Each supplies its own session-list adapter. Discovery remains account-wide; the Editor adapter scopes its list to the workspace's GitHub repositories, or all projects in an empty window, and groups its filters under Cloud. Repository scope applies to cached and connected sessions without changing their routing; opening one preserves its host and session identity and does not provision a replacement. Both windows create sandboxes through the shared contribution's provisioning path, which seeds the created task like a discovered one before connecting. The Editor offers a single `cloud-sandbox` creation target in the harness picker with a repository option group derived from the workspace's GitHub repositories plus "No Repository"; discovered environment providers stay registered for existing conversations but remain excluded from the picker and automatic new-chat selection. On the first send, the Editor provisions the sandbox, reports progress through a cancellable notification, and returns the item under the environment's own session type so the untitled draft rebinds to it. A selected repository resolves the new session's working directory to its GitHub URL for session preparation; "No Repository" explicitly leaves the working directory to the host rather than substituting a local workspace folder.

Sandbox session discovery is window-owned and does not establish host connections. A full refresh reconciles absent disconnected environments; incremental refreshes retain absent entries and reconcile only explicitly removed or replaced tasks. Both preserve connected and provisioning environments. Failed or cancelled scans must not advance incremental discovery progress.
